$comment: tooling/release-lanes.json -- the CLOSED, committed inventory of every evidence lane
this project has (06-13-PLAN.md Task 1, 06-CONTEXT.md D-09/D-14/D-15).
Why closed: tooling/verify-release.mjs asserts that every lane named here appears in a
release manifest EXACTLY ONCE. A lane that vanished from a run is therefore a hard
failure rather than an invisible gap. That assertion is only meaningful if this file is
complete, so a lane the project has and this file omits is itself the defect.
AUTHORITY MODEL (D-09). Continuous integration is authoritative for every lane it can
physically run. A closed set of named lanes -- exactly those carrying a non-null
physicalBlocker below -- is 'local-attested', and a local-attested lane's evidence is
valid ONLY if it records the continuous-integration-attested artefact digest it ran
against.
THE ANTI-LOOPHOLE RULE, stated here so it cannot be argued around later:
NOTHING LOCAL MAY BIND TO LOCALLY BUILT BYTES.
A lane therefore cannot be moved out of continuous integration to make it green, because
the local path requires a continuous-integration artefact to exist first. tooling/
verify-release.mjs enforces this: a local-attested lane reporting PASSED against an
artefact whose builtByRunId is absent or local is a hard failure, proven against the
fixture tooling/fixtures/release-manifest.local-unattested.json.
AN OMITTED LANE READS AS SATISFIED. A lane that genuinely cannot run must therefore emit
an explicit entry with status=BLOCKED (or NOT_RUN_ON_FORK), cases=0 and its stated reason
into the manifest. Silence is never permitted to stand in for a result.
FIELDS
lane            the manifest key; stable, never renamed without updating every manifest.
command         the exact command that produces this lane's evidence.
workflow / job  where continuous integration runs it, or null when it is not wired.
authority       'ci' or 'local-attested'. 'local-attested' iff physicalBlocker is non-null.
physicalBlocker null, or the PHYSICAL reason continuous integration can never run it.
Five lanes carry one. It is not a synonym for 'not wired up yet'.
ciWiring        'wired' when a committed workflow job runs it today, 'unwired' otherwise.
wiringBlocker   null, or why an otherwise-CI-capable lane is not wired today. An unwired
lane reports BLOCKED with this reason; it may never report PASSED.
requiresSecrets true when the lane needs repository secrets, and so reports
NOT_RUN_ON_FORK rather than being absent on a fork-originated run.
owner           the phase number or 'backlog' accountable for closing a non-passing lane. KPL-06 is
the final phase of this milestone, so it may not remain the owner of a lane that is still
BLOCKED at its end -- that is the unowned pattern D-35 exists to kill. Every such owner was
moved to 'backlog' by plan 06-13 Task 3, each with a .planning/WINDOWS.md row.

lanes.physicalBlocker: Row A14 is the only row that changes a system appearance setting WHILE the application is already running and asserts the window re-themes without a relaunch. Delivering that change to a running application requires a logged-in Aqua session whose appearance daemon posts AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification; a hosted GitHub runner has no such session, so the notification is never delivered and the measured window background never changes. This is an observed boundary, not a prediction: at revision 26628e1771d5b90569b5eec232047456fdda9f2e the row reported `status=FAIL cases=4` on macos-15 with `background stayed {"b":0,"g":0,"r":0}` (run 34668212473, job desktop-macos-integration), while the identical row reports `status=PASS cases=4` on a real logged-in session. Rows A10, A12 and A13 pass on the same runner because each applies its setting BEFORE launch; A14 is the only row that cannot.
